function: Excluded, above_phy: federated multiagent D3QN learns network slicing, slice embedding and admission of service requests, not a physical-layer function (p. 5-6, 9-10).
notes: Title and p. 1 abstract: network slicing for satellite direct-to-device links. The agents observe service-request type, embedding-relationship matrix, revenue and substrate network state (p. 5), and the RM agent reward is admission revenue: "Accepting an SR provides a reward equal to the offered revenue of that SR" (p. 6). Results are slice cost, active slices, embedded high-priority requests, slicing capacity, latency and packet loss (Figs. 5-8, Table I, p. 9-10), all slicing and admission outcomes above the physical layer. One sentence says agents "select power levels and channel actions" (p. 5), but no state, reward or result concerns power, channels or beams, so I do not count satellite-link power control as learned. Judgment call for the reviewer: if that sentence is read as learned power or channel control of the satellite link, the NTN rule makes it physical layer, the work would pass above_phy and need grading as area 6. Aggregation is FedAvg at a central server (p. 5), digital, so not area 7.
